name: Cosine
tagline: Semantic search for documentation sites that runs entirely in the browser. No search server, no API key, no query leaves the device.
seoTitle: Cosine – semantic docs search in the browser, without a server
description:
Most docs search either needs a hosted service or matches only exact words: someone who types "how do I get rid of the app" finds nothing on a page called "Uninstall". Cosine closes that gap without a server. `cosine build` splits your Markdown, MDX or HTML pages at their headings and stores a small vector per section next to your site. In the browser, keyword results appear on the first keystroke, and once the embedding model has loaded (about 23 MB, cached) the ranking combines keywords and meaning.

The search field is an accessible web component in English, German, French and Italian that works in any framework, with React bindings on top. Queries are never sent anywhere, and the model can be served from your own domain.

code.title: Build the index, add the field
code.snippet:
<!-- npx cosine build docs --out public/cosine --base-url /docs -->
<script type="module">
  import "@sweberdev/cosine/element"
</script>

<cosine-search index="/cosine/cosine-index.json" lang="de"></cosine-search>

free: Index builder and CLI for Markdown, MDX and built HTML, split at headings with deep links
Hybrid ranking in the browser: BM25 keyword search with prefix matching and typo tolerance, plus cosine similarity on embeddings
Instant keyword results, semantic ranking as soon as the model is loaded, keyword-only for visitors who save data
Scoped search: limit a search field to parts of the site, e.g. only the API reference
Synonym lists stored in the index, so "login" also finds "sign in", even before the model has loaded
Incremental builds in the CLI: --incremental embeds only new and changed sections
Facets: result counts per section of the site, for search pages with filters
Search syntax for visitors: "exact phrases" and -excluded words, also in the semantic ranking
Boosting: rank sections of the site higher or lower, stored in the index
Several indexes in one search field (index="/docs.json /blog.json"), merged into one result list
Facet filter buttons in the web component: a row of sections with counts that narrows the results
Tested in real Chromium on every release: keyboard use, ARIA, narrow screens, reduced motion and an axe-core scan against WCAG 2.1 AA
Benchmarks with fixed limits in CI: bytes per section, bytes per vector and search time over 3000 sections
Frozen public API: a test lists every export, attribute, part and CLI option, so 1.x cannot break them silently
Guides for migrating from Pagefind, Orama, MiniSearch and Lunr, framework recipes, troubleshooting and a nightly real-model test
Compact int8 vectors: about 400 bytes per section
Accessible <cosine-search> web component (ARIA combobox) in English, German, French and Italian
React component and hooks, English or multilingual models, model self-hosting for GDPR and FADP
pro: Vite plugin: the index builds itself in Vite, Astro, VitePress, SvelteKit and Nuxt, and in dev
Embedding cache: a rebuild embeds only the sections that changed
Next.js integration: the index is built from the prerendered pages after next build, kept in .next/cache so CI rebuilds embed only what changed
Algolia migration: cosine-migrate turns a DocSearch export and its synonyms into a Cosine index, no new crawl
Search insights without tracking: queries without results, results nobody opened, as HTML, Markdown or CSV
Insights trends: new and resolved gaps, rising queries and a weekly chart, compared with the period before
Gap suggestions: for every query without results, whether it is a typo, which pages come closest, or that a page is missing (cosine-insights suggest)
Weekly search report: a ready-made GitHub Action opens trends and gaps as an issue every Monday
Short answers: cosine-answers quotes the sentence that answers the question above the results, without an LLM
Insights dashboard: one HTML file with overview, gaps with fixes, weekly trends, top content and CSV downloads

faq.q: Does it need a server or an API key?
faq.a: No. The index is a static file next to your site and the model runs in the visitor's browser through transformers.js.
The library is about 7 KB gzip. The index needs about 400 bytes per section. The English model is about 23 MB, loaded only when the search field gets focus and then cached by the browser.

faq.q: Is it compliant with the GDPR and the Swiss FADP?
faq.a: Queries never leave the browser. The model is downloaded from Hugging Face by default; serve it from your own domain if that request is a problem for your site. Keyword-only mode contacts no third party at all.

faq.q: Does it work with German, French or Italian docs?
faq.a: Keyword search works in every language and folds accents and ß. For semantic search in these languages use the multilingual model, which also matches queries and pages in different languages.
Any. The search field is a web component; the index is built from Markdown, MDX or the HTML your site generator produces. React bindings are included, and Cosine Pro adds a Vite plugin.

faq.q: Can I use the open-source part on its own?
faq.a: Yes. @sweberdev/cosine and @sweberdev/cosine-react are MIT-licensed and complete without Pro.
